quote: my wife and I are looking at having to spend money on a roof right now, and our electric bill's kinda high.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly states they need to spend money on a roof soon - a textbook roofing cross-sell trigger - but the rep never bridges to Ion's in-house roofing team.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have intended to address roof later given the roof question came at 03:12, but that question was purely qualifying (type/age), not a roofing-sale bridge.
coaching_implication: Rep should have said something like 'Ion actually does roofing in-house - we could look at bundling that with solar' immediately when the customer mentioned needing a new roof.

quote: my my dad and I have kinda dabbled solar panels trying to run my pool pump and stuff.
stewart_read: DIY solar experimentation plus a pool pump is a strong qualification and interest signal - a technically curious, motivated customer.
coaching_implication: Rep should have leaned into this as a hook ('so you already know a bit about how this works') to build rapport and curiosity rather than letting it pass silently.

quote: If power outages happen, it'd be nice to be maybe a little self sufficient.
stewart_read: Customer directly raises backup power interest, which maps to Ion's Tesla Powerwall offering, but the rep never mentions battery as an option.
alternative_hypothesis: The call may have been cut short by the DQ before battery could be raised, but the topic came at 02:14, minutes before the DQ moment at 04:27 - there was time.
coaching_implication: Flag the outage/self-sufficiency comment and mention Powerwall exists as an option the closer can walk through.

quote: I was taking a look at the, the across the street neighbors there, and it does look like they have shade pretty close to the house
stewart_read: Rep performs a detailed technical/satellite analysis comparing the neighbor's shading and system sizing - closer-tier design content delivered by the setter.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a legitimate reassurance technique to address fear, but the depth (discussing offset, shading, southern exposure) crosses into product/design explanation that belongs to the closer.
coaching_implication: Redirect this reassurance to a lighter version: acknowledge the fear, note that every home is designed individually, and let the closer walk through specifics.

alternative_hypothesis: The DQ concern (Edisto net metering) surfaced almost immediately after, which may have preempted any planned flip - but the rep had the opening to flip before checking net metering.

quote: it just looks like we might not be able to help you at the moment
stewart_read: Call ends with a vague promise to check with the design team and call back, no date/time, no explicit next step owned by the rep.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be legitimate DQ handling if Edisto genuinely has no net metering program, in which case ending is correct procedure - but even so, the close lacked any firm structure (e.g., 'I'll call you by Friday').
coaching_implication: Even on a probable DQ, give a concrete timeframe for the callback so the customer isn't left with an open loop.
